One-time steps on the handheld and the PC

Streaming over the cable needs no Wi-Fi and no internet.

RETROID POCKET (USB tethering is turned off on its Android, so we use the USB bridge)
On the handheld, once:
1. Settings → About device → tap Build number 7 times.
2. Settings → System → Developer options → turn on USB debugging.
On the PC, once:
3. Install Apollo (or Sunshine).
4. Get ArtemisPocket-PC-Tools from the Pocket Nexus GitHub page and double-click ArtemisPocket-USB-Bridge.bat. It downloads ADB if needed and can start with Windows.
Every time:
5. Plug the cable in (allow USB debugging the first time) and open Pocket Nexus. It finds the PC on its own. The first time, pair with the PIN in Apollo's web page.

OTHER HANDHELDS WITH USB TETHERING
Turn on USB tethering (Settings → Network → Hotspot & tethering) and run ArtemisPocket-USB-Setup.bat on the PC once.

Tips: the bridge carries up to about 60 Mbps; lower the USB-C bitrate if the picture stutters. The handheld charges from the PC while you play.

What the Xbox button opens on Windows

The Guide (Xbox) button goes to the PC as a controller button. Steam Big Picture and Xbox-app games react to it.

The Windows Game Bar only opens from Guide when "Open Xbox Game Bar using this button on a controller" is on (Windows Settings → Gaming → Xbox Game Bar), and with some virtual controllers it doesn't react at all.

If you want the Game Bar every time, set the button to "Xbox Game Bar (Win+G)" instead: it sends the keyboard shortcut, which always works.
